title: Cerulean Systems - Ops immersion and incident playbook kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Cerulean's onboarding focused on ops immersion, incident playbook creation, and network connectivity for a private deployment. Discussed timelines, success criteria, security must-haves (SOC2, KMS, SSO), and next steps for a two-week pilot. Agreed to run a baseline latency/cost benchmark and share security pack and ramp playbook.
transcript:
Meeting header: Recorded 2026-05-26 14:00 PDT, Duration ~62 minutes. Attendees listed above.

[00:00] Avery Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining from Cerulean, um we wanted to make this a practical ops immersion, we're gonna walk through the runbook, the incident playbook, and the pilot plan. 
[00:16] Maya Lopez: thanks Avery. quick context — Cerulean's platform handles realtime route optimization, so latency is like, top of mind. we've been running inference on-prem for our core scheduler but looking to move to a private redwood deployment.
[00:32] Diego Martinez: awesome. just to set expectations: private deployment for us means customer-managed VPC and the redwood control plane in our account, correct? or do you want the on-prem bundle?
[00:44] Maya Lopez: initial ask is VPC with a private control plane; on-prem might come later for regulatory nodes.
[00:51] Ethan Park: and we have strict egress rules — traffic needs to stay inside the VPC except for telemetry to our observability stack.
[00:59] Priya Kapoor: noted. we'll flag that in the runbook and link the network diagrams in the kickoff pack.
[01:08] Samira Nadeem: quick security checklist: SOC 2 is required, we need KMS integration for keys, SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning, and audit logs retained for 13 months. any gotchas?
[01:21] Diego Martinez: we support KMS/HSM integrations and SAML SSO; audit logs and retention are configurable. i'll double-check the retention windows — sometimes the export names in the control plane are slightly different in the current UI.
[01:35] Maya Lopez: ok thanks. also curious about the model variants and cost controls — we want to cap spend during the pilot.
[01:44] Avery Chen: absolutely. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization profiles; but for private deployments we'll surface recommended profiles and a cost forecast.
[01:55] Jordan Blake: can we do a hard cap? like alert if forecasted monthly run rate exceeds X?
[02:02] Priya Kapoor: yes — billing alerts and token-level cost breakdowns are available. for private, we can integrate cost reporting with your FinOps dashboards; we'll include an example alert rule in the pack.
[02:15] [00:02:15] Ethan Park: on infra sizing — what GPU families are validated for the runtime? we prefer A10s but also have some A100 pools.
[02:26] Diego Martinez: the runtime supports Ampere/A100 and we have validated kernel paths for both; sequence length and KV cache behavior differs, so we'll recommend instance types based on your token distribution.
[02:39] Maya Lopez: our scheduler typically generates 1024 tokens per request at peaks; so throughput matters.
[02:48] Diego Martinez: got it. we usually recommend dedicated pools with continuous batching for that workload; i'll include throughput estimates.
[02:58] [00:02:58] Samira Nadeem: incident response — i want an on-call runbook for model regressions and for CPU/GPU flapping. do you have templated playbooks?
[03:10] Avery Chen: yes, we have incident templates: degraded-latency, model-quality-regression, and infra-flapping. today we'll do a walkthrough of a stub playbook and we'll tailor it during sprint zero.
[03:23] Jordan Blake: can we tie incident alerts to our pager rota? we use OpsGenie.
[03:29] Priya Kapoor: OpsGenie and PagerDuty are supported; we'll map alert severities to your routing rules.
[03:36] [00:03:36] Ethan Park: let's talk timeline. Cerulean wants pilot in two weeks — realistic?
[03:43] Avery Chen: two-week baseline pilot is tight but doable if we scope narrowly: deploy private control plane, provision one model, run synthetic latency benchmarks and a small traffic mirror.
[03:54] Diego Martinez: that would require pre-approved VPC peering and service endpoints; if Cerulean's infra team can open the needed subnets and IAM roles this week we can target 2 weeks.
[04:05] Maya Lopez: we can carve out the subnets by EOD Friday, and Samira will coordinate the IAM policy.
[04:12] Samira Nadeem: yes, we'll do that. what's required for the KV cache and persistent store?
[04:18] Diego Martinez: KV cache is in-memory on the GPUs; persistent artifacts like model weights live in object storage. for private we support S3-compatible endpoints — we'll need an IAM role and a signed bucket policy.
[04:30] [00:04:30] Samira Nadeem: perfect. about compliance docs: can you share SOC 2 cert and your pen test summary?
[04:36] Priya Kapoor: yes, we'll share a security pack (SOC2 cert, pen test summary, dataflow diagram). i also have a short questionnaire for hosting controls; i'll drop that after the call.
[04:48] Jordan Blake: any performance gotchas with KV caching and long-running sessions? we rely on long KV sequences for conversation-like state.
[04:56] Diego Martinez: the runtime manages KV eviction heuristics; for long sessions we advise sticky routing to the same pool to keep caches warm. there's a tradeoff — sticky routing can lower multiplexing efficiency.
[05:10] Maya Lopez: that tradeoff is fine as long as latency stays under 80ms p95.
[05:17] Diego Martinez: we'll run p95-focused tests in the pilot.
[05:23] [00:05:23] Avery Chen: ok recap so far: Cerulean will prepare network + IAM by Friday; Redwood will provide security pack, pilot runbook, and a staging checklist. we'll also produce throughput/lantency estimates for A10 vs A100.
[05:40] Maya Lopez: note: our legal prefers data residency logs to be kept in-country for EU nodes, but primary pilot is US-west.
[05:49] Samira Nadeem: we also have a requirement for encrypted backups with keys managed by our KMS — no managed keys.
[05:56] Priya Kapoor: noted — customer-managed KMS is supported; i'll add the key rotation and custody docs.
[06:04] [00:06:04] Ethan Park: what about rollback and failover? if we push a model that regresses, what's the canary path?
[06:14] Diego Martinez: rollouts support automatic canary windows, A/B splits, and immediate rollback to pinned model versions. the control plane exposes a rollback API and we can template a runbook to execute it.
[06:27] Jordan Blake: we'd want an automatic fallback to a lighter quantized variant when latency spikes. does Redwood support auto-fallbacks by policy?
[06:36] Avery Chen: yes — smart routing policies can fallback by model tier or region. we'll include a sample policy for your use case.
[06:44] [00:06:44] Samira Nadeem: last-minute question: audit logs, are they tamper-evident? we need chain-of-custody for certain events.
[06:54] Diego Martinez: logs can be exported to your SIEM and we sign them with an append-only digest; i'll send the documentation page, but i want to confirm the exact retention and export format.
[07:07] Maya Lopez: cool.
[07:11] [00:07:11] Priya Kapoor: action items and next steps we'll surface in the follow-up email. quick note — Diego will run a synthetic benchmark plan and share results in a spreadsheet link (shared: /links/cerulean-pilot-benchmark-2026.xlsx).
[07:26] Ethan Park: thanks, please include request/response traces so we can sanity check topology.
[07:32] Diego Martinez: yea i'll include traces and example payloads.
[07:36] [00:07:36] Jordan Blake: can we get a runbook template for incident triage? ideally something that ties severity to steps and to responsible roles.
[07:45] Avery Chen: yep — we'll provide triage templates and a mapping to your on-call rosters.
[07:51] Samira Nadeem: we'll also want a pre-mortem session after the pilot.
[07:56] Maya Lopez: +1.
[08:00] [00:08:00] Priya Kapoor: last thing — pricing model for the pilot: we'll send a pilot quote that includes reserved capacity for two weeks and optional overage caps.
[08:10] Maya Lopez: prefer a committed minimum for the pilot with a hard cap.
[08:14] Avery Chen: understood — we'll draft a two-week committed quote with a hard cap option.
[08:20] [00:08:20] Diego Martinez: any more technical Qs? if not i'll note we need your VPC peering details and preferred GPU families.
[08:27] Ethan Park: no more. we'll email the subnets and IAM role ARNs.
[08:31] [00:08:31] Avery Chen: great. recap of next steps then, we'll follow up with a kickoff pack and security docs, Diego will run benchmarks, Priya will send the questionnaire and pilot quote, Cerulean will provision networking and IAM by EOD Friday.
[08:49] Maya Lopez: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:53] [00:08:53] End of transcript.

Notes about transcript: some speaker labels auto-assigned (Speaker 1/2 alternation in a few spots), minor transcription errors on product names (e.g., "Redwood Private" transcribed as "red wood private" in one segment).

Shared artifacts referenced: Cerulean VPC diagram (link shared in chat), /links/cerulean-pilot-benchmark-2026.xlsx, security-pack-v1.pdf (to be shared), pilot-quote-draft.pdf (to be shared).
